expectation_label: Refusing an invitation requires an explanation

experience.narrative: A colleague invited me to dinner after work. I thanked her and said I couldn't attent, without giving a reason. She asked whether something was wrong and seemed uncomfortable when I repeated that I couldn't make it.

evidence.content: The colleague asked whether something was wrong after the invitation was declined.
The contributor interpreted the colleague's response as discomfort with the unexplained refusal.

expectation_label: Declining an invitation does not require justification

experience.narrative: After a project meeting, a colleague invited me to dinner with the rest of the team. I thanked her and said I wouldn't be joining them. She smiled, said 'No problem, maybe next time,' and continued discussing the restaurant with the others. Nobody asked why I wasn't coming. I interpreted her response as an indication that declining the invitation was acceptable without explaining my reasons.

relationship.value: Colleagues working on the same project

evidence.content: The colleague accepted the refusal, suggested another occasion, and did not request an explanation.
The narrator interpreted the interaction as indicating that a refusal did not require justification.

expectation_label: Silence during disagreement can preserve interpersonal harmony

experience.narrative: During a family dinner, my aunt and uncle disagreed about how to organise an upcoming celebration. When my uncle raised his voice, I stopped contributing to the discussion. Later, my aunt thanked me for not making the disagreement more confrontational. I interpreted her comment as appreciation for my decision to remain silent rather than escalate the argument.

evidence.content: The narrator stopped contributing after the uncle raised his voice, and the aunt later thanked the narrator for avoiding confrontation.
The narrator interpreted the aunt's response as approval of silence as a way to prevent escalation.

expectation_label: Silence during disagreement can be interpreted as disengagement

experience.narrative: My friend and I disagreed about a decision we had made together. When the conversation became tense, I stopped responding because I needed time to think. My friend asked whether I was deliberately ignoring her and said she felt I was shutting her out. I explained that I had gone quiet because I was overwhelmed. I interpreted her reaction as an expectation that I remain verbally engaged even during a difficult conversation.

evidence.content: The friend asked whether the narrator was ignoring her and said she felt shut out.
The narrator interpreted the friend's reaction as an expectation of continued verbal engagement during disagreement.

expectation_label: A host should express hospitality by covering a guest's expenses

experience.narrative: A friend visiting my city for the first time joined me for lunch. When the bill arrived, I immediately offered to pay for both of us. She reached for her wallet, but I told her that she was my guest. She thanked me and accepted. I felt that covering the meal was part of welcoming her, rather than something I expected her to repay.

evidence.content: The narrator offered to cover the entire bill, identified the friend as a guest, and the friend accepted.
The narrator understood paying as an expression of hospitality rather than an expectation of repayment.

expectation_label: Paying for someone can establish an informal expectation of reciprocity

experience.narrative: After finishing a project together, I offered to pay for my colleague's lunch. She accepted and said she would get the next one. When we met again a week later, she insisted on paying and reminded me that I had covered our previous meal. I interpreted our exchange as a way of maintaining balance through alternating acts of generosity.

setting.value: Lunch between colleagues after a completed project

evidence.content: The colleague promised to pay for the next lunch and subsequently did so.
The narrator interpreted the exchange as an informal practice of reciprocal generosity.

expectation_label: Reducing direct eye contact can communicate deference to seniority

experience.narrative: During a meeting with a senior colleague, I listened carefully but avoided maintaining direct eye contact for long periods. Afterwards, another colleague commented that I had appeared particularly respectful and attentive. I explained that I had been conscious of the senior colleague's position and had deliberately kept my gaze less direct. I interpreted the comment as recognition of my attempt to show deference.

setting.value: Professional meeting with a senior colleague

evidence.content: The narrator avoided sustained eye contact and another colleague described the behaviour as respectful.
The narrator associated reduced eye contact with showing respect for seniority.

expectation_label: Avoiding eye contact can be interpreted as interpersonal discomfort

experience.narrative: I met a close friend for coffee after we had disagreed earlier in the week. While she talked, I repeatedly looked down at the table rather than meeting her eyes. She eventually asked whether I was uncomfortable being around her. I told her that I was still thinking about our disagreement. I interpreted her question as an indication that she associated my lack of eye contact with unresolved tension.

setting.value: Private conversation at a café after a disagreement

evidence.content: The narrator repeatedly looked down and the friend asked whether the narrator felt uncomfortable.
The narrator understood the friend's question as connecting reduced eye contact with interpersonal discomfort.

expectation_label: Refusing an offering can be interpreted as rejecting the giver's care

experience.narrative: During a visit to my aunt's home, she offered me a plate of food she had prepared. I thanked her but declined because I had already eaten. She looked disappointed and asked whether I disliked her cooking. I reassured her that I appreciated the effort. I interpreted her reaction as concern that my refusal meant I did not value her hospitality.

setting.value: Family visit at a relative's home

evidence.content: The aunt asked whether the narrator disliked her cooking after the food was declined.
The narrator interpreted the reaction as concern that the refusal communicated a lack of appreciation.

expectation_label: Refusing an offering can be interpreted as rejecting the giver's care

experience.narrative: A friend gave me a small handmade bracelet for my birthday. I told her it was thoughtful but said I could not accept it because I rarely wore jewellery. She became quiet and later told me she had spent several evenings making it. I realised that she might have understood my refusal as a rejection of the care she had put into the gift.

evidence.content: The friend became quiet after the gift was declined and later described the effort involved in making it.
The narrator considered whether declining the gift had been interpreted as rejecting the friend's care.

expectation_label: Making oneself available can be interpreted as evidence of relational commitment

experience.narrative: My friend sent me several messages about a difficult day, but I did not respond until the following evening because I had been overwhelmed with work. When I finally replied, she said she had felt unimportant to me. I explained that my delay was not intentional. I interpreted her reaction as connecting responsiveness with how much I valued our friendship.

setting.value: Private messaging during a stressful period

evidence.content: The friend said she felt unimportant after receiving a delayed reply.
The narrator interpreted the reaction as associating timely responses with friendship commitment.

expectation_label: Making oneself available can be interpreted as evidence of relational commitment

experience.narrative: I attended a friend's graduation celebration but left after an hour because I had an early shift the next morning. The following day, she told me she had hoped I would stay longer and that my early departure made her feel the occasion was not important to me. I explained my work schedule. I interpreted her disappointment as an expectation that close friends demonstrate support by making time for important events.

evidence.content: The friend said the narrator's early departure made the celebration seem unimportant.
The narrator interpreted staying at important events as one way of demonstrating relational commitment.

expectation_label: Respect for social hierarchy can be communicated through formal acknowledgment

experience.narrative: At my new workplace, I addressed a senior manager by her first name during a meeting. Afterwards, a colleague suggested that I use her professional title until she invited me to be less formal. I had intended to sound approachable, but I interpreted the advice as indicating that formal address was an expected acknowledgment of professional seniority.

evidence.content: A colleague advised the narrator to use the senior manager's professional title.
The narrator interpreted formal address as a way to acknowledge professional hierarchy.

expectation_label: Respect for social hierarchy can be communicated through formal acknowledgment

experience.narrative: During a departmental meeting, an older senior colleague entered the room while I remained seated. Afterwards, a coworker quietly explained that people in our team usually stood briefly when that colleague arrived. I had not intended any disrespect. I interpreted the coworker's advice as suggesting that standing was a recognised way of acknowledging seniority in that workplace.

evidence.content: A coworker explained that team members usually stood when the senior colleague entered.
The narrator interpreted standing as a formal acknowledgment of seniority.

expectation_label: Personal involvement can be understood as an expression of care

experience.narrative: At a family gathering, my uncle asked several questions about my job search, salary expectations, and future plans. I initially felt uncomfortable discussing these details. Later, he offered to introduce me to someone in his professional network. I began to interpret his questions as an attempt to understand my situation so he could help, although I still preferred to keep some details private.

evidence.content: The uncle asked detailed career questions and later offered a professional introduction.
The narrator considered the questions a possible expression of practical concern while maintaining a preference for privacy.

expectation_label: Personal involvement can be understood as an expression of care

experience.narrative: I mentioned to my older sister that I was having difficulty managing my university workload. Without being asked, she suggested a study schedule, recommended speaking to my tutor, and offered to review my assignments. I felt slightly overwhelmed by the advice because I had only wanted someone to listen. She later explained that offering solutions was how she tried to support me. I understood her intentions while recognising that her approach did not match what I needed.

evidence.content: The sister offered several practical suggestions without being asked and later explained that she intended to help.
The narrator interpreted the unsolicited advice as an attempted expression of care despite finding it overwhelming.
